sections.heading: 1. Set the height, grip with hands
lines: ① Leave 2–3 finger widths under the armpit.
② Handles at wrist height, elbows soft.
③ Keep wrists straight, push through palms.
④ Take small steps and rest often.

caption:
After hurting her ankle, Lulu is commuting on crutches. A few days in, her shoulders and wrists hurt more than her ankle.

Leaning your armpits on the tops of the crutches can load up your shoulders and arms. Your weight is meant to go through your hands on the handles.

Hybi's tip: leave 2–3 finger widths under the armpit, set the handles at wrist height and keep your wrists straight. Take small steps and rest often, and follow your treating team's advice on how much weight to put through the leg.

Tingling fingers or a leg that's getting more swollen are worth an assessment. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help. Book online via the link in bio 🩼
